items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: he in 1927 wrote a piece about me in the DownBeat, highly praising my playing, but then Mezzrow went over there to see him... and Pernassie just turned from our group... and went along with Mezzrow

ctx.x: '38, yes, but never -- you know, I think those were the first polls and I was getting, you know, a lot of popularity. You notice that the men who did win the polls, with all due respect to their being great players, are pretty much in the limelight, have a big act going or they're with a big band and they're being featured, as I was in those early days, '37 with Dorsey and '38 with Goodman.
Well, what about in Europe. What about Panassie and people like that. They often make awards, the French Hot Tub and so on. Were you involved in any of those?

No, I don't think -- there was a very odd thing about Pernasia (phonetic) he in 1927 wrote a piece about me in the DownBeat, highly praising my playing, but then Mezzrow went over there to see him and told him some funny things, and Pernassie just turned from our group, which he liked very much, the group that made Nobody's Sweetheart and all that, and went along with Mezzrow, and never said another word about me.
